name: maybe_Gfx_ModelPart_AllocSlots
signature: void maybe_Gfx_ModelPart_AllocSlots(GfxModelPart* part, u32 base, u32 count, u32 size, u8 mode)
summary: Carves a model instance's per-part slot arrays out of the resource buffer at base: 16-byte-aligns size, reserves count 0x448-byte and 0xD0-byte per-slot tables, then default-constructs the 0x20-byte elements of every 0x100-byte block. The caller passes a null destination, so the first parameter is damaged.
evidence: The only caller is now Gfx_ModelInstance_BuildSubBlocks (0.50), which passes the same count/size/base it uses for its 0x448-byte sub-block layout. That call passes 0 for the destination while the body writes self+0x14, so the decompiled first parameter (and therefore the 'model part' class identity) is not proven; kept at 0.45.

name: Sound_StreamGroup_Init
summary: One-time initialisation of a stream's four voice slots: stores the owner id at +0x08 and sets each 0x10-byte slot's voice-stealing threshold to 'never' (0x7FFFFFFF) for the first slot and 1 for the rest, then marks +0x58 initialised. Called from Sound_Stream_SetSource when a stream first receives a source.
evidence: Caller is now the confident Sound_Stream_SetSource (0x0054260C), which binds the source and calls this once; the +0x58 initialised guard, the fixed four 0x10-byte slots and the call into Sound_Voice_SelectLowestPriority match a per-stream voice-group setup. The 'group' struct layout is still structural, hence 0.5 rather than higher.

name: Sound_3D_CalcPanFromMatrix
summary: Builds a rotation matrix from the caller's matrix and forwards it to Sound_3D_CalcPan, the matrix-based variant of the 3D pan calculation used by Sound_3D_CalcAttenuation.
evidence: Caller is now the confident Sound_3D_CalcAttenuation (0x00542C54) and the callee the confident Sound_3D_CalcPan (0x0054353C); the single call in the body feeds a locally built matrix straight into the pan calculator. Ghidra dropped every argument (the signature is empty), so the direction/pan role is confirmed but the exact parameters are not.

name: maybe_Sound_Voice_ReleaseChannels
summary: Tears a voice down: stops and frees every channel in the voice's channel array except keepChannel, clears the voice state, unlinks it from the mixer list and invokes the owner callback with reason 3. The parameter order of the old name was backwards: the voice is the second argument and the first is the one channel to keep.
evidence: The body indexes the second argument as the voice (channel array at +0, count at +8, callback pointer at +0xC) and only compares the first argument against individual channel pointers, so the previous '(keep, stream)' model was inverted. There is no direct caller (vtable/callback slot) and the final callback(voice, 3, arg) is a teardown notification, so the exact use stays at 0.45.

name: Sound_Driver_ReleaseAllSeqChannels
summary: Shutdown helper: when the driver is running (+0x10), releases every note in the driver's intrusive sequence-channel list and then releases the channel-pool buffer, clearing the running flag. Called only from Sound_System_Shutdown.
evidence: Caller is now the confident Sound_System_Shutdown (0x00542580) and the per-node callee the confident Sound_SeqNote_Release (0x0055614C); iterating the driver's intrusive list, releasing each node and then the pool buffer is the sequence-channel teardown. The pool helper 0x00556C04 is still unnamed, so 'channels' (rather than 'notes') is inferred from the list node type.

name: maybe_Sound_Player_Reset
summary: Resets a player to its idle state: unlinks its two driver-queue nodes, finishes and frees any playing note, clears the active/volume flags, releases the pending file request and detaches the driver-registry node. Its only caller, Sound_Player_Ctor, calls it to clean a reused player, so it is not a plain 'stop'.
evidence: The sole caller is now the confident Sound_Player_Ctor (0x00550744), which calls it before initialising the player's own fields; every branch here is teardown of leftover state (queue nodes, note, fs request, flags), while a real stop would not be called from the constructor. Kept below 0.5 because indirect stop/restart uses cannot be excluded.

name: maybe_Gfx_SamplerState_Write
summary: Writes a three-byte PICA200 texture-sampler state into the draw command stream: mode 0 sets filter 1 / 0x80 / wrap 6, modes 1 and 2 swap the filter and wrap bytes, then the bytes are appended after the element command and the stream cursor at state+4 is updated.
evidence: Callers are now the generic draw-submit paths Gfx_SubmitSortedElement (0x002D4604) and Gfx_Overlay_SubmitQuad (0x0055D428), not a model instance, and state+4 holds a command-stream cursor; the mode switch only chooses the three sampler bytes (1/0x80/6) which 0x00656ACC appends. The emitting callee Gfx_Pica_EmitDrawElements is itself low-confidence, so the name stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Model_BuildAimPartList
signature: void maybe_Model_BuildAimPartList(u32 owner, u32 partA, u32 partB, u32 partC)
summary: Builds the aim-part descriptors for Model_AttachAimParts: copies the owner/part ids into locals and default-constructs two 0x40-byte descriptors in a 428-byte stack buffer. Ghidra lost the remaining ~1.4 KB of the function, so the descriptor contents stay unknown.
evidence: No new named evidence beyond the caller Model_AttachAimParts (0x00222E90); the only visible call is std_ConstructArray(buf, 0x00535B54, 0x40, 2), which shows two 0x40-byte descriptors but not what they contain. The body is truncated after the prologue, hence the low confidence.

name: maybe_Fs_Entry_Dtor
summary: Destructor of a cache entry: erases the entry's intrusive node range from its container and, when +0x14 is set, also erases the entry's red-black-tree node, then returns the entry pointer (vtable destructor convention).
evidence: The erase calls now resolve to Container_List_EraseAllNodes (0x00707E0C) and std_RbTree_EraseNode (0x0010EC14), matching a two-container destructor that returns its argument. There is still no named caller (it is a vtable slot), and 0x0010EAB0 reached through this body is badly named, so the 'Fs_Entry' class stays unproven.

name: Battle2DUnit_PartyMember_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the 2D battle party-member unit: runs the Battle2DUnit base constructor, installs vtable 0x0077E80C, initialises the instance state at +0x17DC..+0x17E4 and constructs the embedded Field_GameObject at +0x17E8.
evidence: The base constructor is the confident Battle2DUnit_Ctor (0x00483D04); vtable 0x0077E80C contains FieldParty_ResetMemberSlot (0x001FF200) and maybe_Battle2DUnit_BindPartyMember (0x0059F36C), i.e. the party-member 2D unit, and the tail constructs a Field_GameObject child. That is stronger than the previous 'UI child object' reading.

name: maybe_std_InitStaticArray
summary: Compiler-generated static initialiser: default-constructs an 8-element array of 4-byte elements from type descriptor 0x005906C0 in a 768-byte stack buffer. Ghidra marks the constructor call as non-returning, so the rest of the initialiser and its purpose are unrecoverable.
evidence: Callers are now Ui_SkillPanel_AdvanceNodeSequence and maybe_Ui_SceneFlow_CommitScene, i.e. unrelated UI paths, and the only callee is still std_ConstructArray; that fits a guarded one-time static array initialiser rather than a UI routine. Type 0x005906C0 and the lost tail keep it generic, so 0.30.

name: maybe_Field2D_Actor_RebuildTask
summary: Replaces an actor's task object at +0x88: releases the old task through its vtable, constructs a new task from the state block at +0x38 via Field2D_Task_Init and stores the result back. Called from Field2D_Step_WaitTime, so it is the task-swap path, not a one-off creator.
evidence: Caller is now the confident Field2D_Step_WaitTime (0x005BE768) and the callee Field2D_Task_Init (0x005C89A0); the body destroys the old +0x88 object before constructing the replacement, which is why 'CreateTask' was misleading. The arg2 forwarding is partly extraout_r1, so the parameter list stays uncertain.

name: maybe_Field2D_Sprite_SetAppearanceFromCharId
signature: void maybe_Field2D_Sprite_SetAppearanceFromCharId(u32* self, u32 object, u32 arg3, int charId)
summary: Chooses a 2D sprite's appearance (direction frame, palette and draw params) from a character id: looks the id up in the character record table, falls back to the neutral frame 0xFF, and re-resolves the draw params through Field2D_Sprite_ComputeDrawParams before storing the packed result.
evidence: The character-record lookup func_0063B944 (called on object+8) and the fallback 0xFF are unchanged and the named callee Field2D_Sprite_ComputeDrawParams supplies the frame, but there is still no direct caller (vtable/callback use) and the trailing arg5/arg6/arg7 are unnamed, so the 'set appearance' reading stays at 0.45.

name: maybe_Field2D_Sprite_AdvancePathStep
summary: Per-frame 2D sprite path update: decrements the step counter at +0x38, then for each of the two path fields at +0x2D0/+0x2D4 chooses a path step and rebuilds the corresponding task object, finally asking the sprite's vtable to apply the updated position.
evidence: The caller is now the confident Field2D_Sprite_CheckViewBounds (0x005CA31C) and the callee maybe_Field2D_Sprite_ChoosePathStep; the body decrements a counter and swaps task objects for the two path programs, which fits movement but does not prove 'advance one step'. Kept below 0.5.

name: maybe_Ui_Context_SetStatePair
summary: Forwards (0, 2) to vtable slot +0x28 of the UI core's state controller (Ui_GetCore()->f_14->f_10). The same 60-byte shape as 0x005D9EE0, which calls slot +0x1C with (0), identifies it as a UI state-controller setter, not a field-gimmick state machine.
evidence: Both the callee Ui_GetCore and the sibling 0x005D9EE0 (R2_018, same controller, slot +0x1C) are named; the vtable slot +0x28 and the constant pair (0,2) are visible. No callers exist, so what the pair means and which UI mode it selects remains unknown; kept at 0.35.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_UpdateSelectionCursor
signature: void maybe_Field_Gimmick_UpdateSelectionCursor(FieldGimmick* self, int* arg2, int* arg3)
summary: Per-frame cursor upkeep: when no UI window is open (UI core +0xD84 < 1) it drops the gimmick's handle, and when the stored reference at +0x14 has gone stale it calls the context virtual +0x14 and clears +0x20; either way it then ticks the target marker at +0x1D7C.
evidence: The caller is now maybe_Ui_SceneFlow_UpdateCursorAndSprite and the callees Field_Gimmick_TickHandleRef / maybe_Battle_TextWindow_UpdateTargetMarker are named, which supports cursor/marker upkeep; however the class owning +0x1D7C is still ambiguous (the marker helper is battle-flavoured), so the Field_Gimmick label stays at 0.45.

name: Field_NpcAction_GetJumpSpeedById
summary: Looks up a field NPC motion parameter record by 16-bit id (Data_LookupSubRecord on the manager's +0x87C table) and returns a speed scaled by the record's kind byte at +0x12: kinds 1..4 multiply the base speed by 0.1, 0.3, 0.5 and 0.8; other kinds return the base speed unchanged.
evidence: Assembly at 0x005E8218..0x005E8284 (verified with look.py) is `ldrb r0,[r0,#0x12]; cmp 1..4; vldreq s0,[base]; vldreq s1,[const 0.1/0.3/0.5/0.8]; vmul.f32 s0,s0,s1; pop {r3,r4,r5,pc}`. That is the Ghidra VFP s0 return-drop trap (the C body shows no return), and the caller Field_NpcAction_Jump uses it for jump speed, so the old 'Actor_LookupByIdB' missed both the returned float and the NPC-action caller.

name: maybe_Data_GetFirstRowB
summary: Fourteen-instruction getter with its return value dropped by Ghidra: resolves Game_GetDataManager and returns the first row of the manager's +0x884 sub-record table via 0x0063F7BC. Byte-identical to 0x005E889C and the other copies at 0x005E88D4/0x005E88F0.
evidence: Disassembly of 0x0063F7BC (look.py) is a pure getter: `ldr r0,[r0,#0x884]; ... ldr r0,[r0,#0x58]; ... bx lr`, no side effects, so the old 'NotifyGlobal' wording described a notification that does not happen. Callers Field_NpcAction_Jump / maybe_Anim_ClipSlot_InitLinearMotion just consume the row pointer that Ghidra dropped; which table +0x884 is stays unknown.

name: maybe_Data_GetFirstRowA
summary: Fourteen-instruction getter whose return value Ghidra dropped: resolves Game_GetDataManager and returns the first row of the manager's +0x884 sub-record table via 0x0063F7BC. One of four identical copies (0x005E889C/0x005E88B8/0x005E88D4/0x005E88F0).
evidence: 0x0063F7BC is a pure table getter (manager+0x884 -> head row, bx lr) with no writes, identical twin of 0x005E88B8; caller Field_NpcJumpAction_Setup only consumes the row pointer. So 'NotifyGlobal' was wrong, but neither the table at +0x884 nor the dropped return type is identifiable, hence 0.35.

name: maybe_Sound_StreamPlayer_InitLock
signature: void maybe_Sound_StreamPlayer_InitLock(SoundStreamPlayer* player, u32 mode, int channelCount, int arg4)
summary: One-time start/lock setup for stream players, called from Sound_InitPlayers: if the player flag bit 0 is clear, a channel count was requested and the global lock is free, it initialises the critical section at 0x007C8650 and records a handle. The tail was lost to bad instruction data, so the unlock path is unknown.
evidence: The caller is now the confident Sound_InitPlayers (0x001EB470), which contradicts 'StartLocked' (this is called during player-pool init) and the callee Os_InitCriticalSection confirms the lock side. Ghidra truncates both branches with halt_baddata, so the actual completion path cannot be checked; kept at 0.30.

name: Save_CopyChecksumTable
summary: Copies the static 512-byte save/check-digit table at 0x0072E93C through a stack buffer into the caller's buffer and returns it. Called from the save crypto context init and from both check-digit generation and verification, so the table is part of the save-code checksum path.
evidence: All three callers are now named and all are save-code crypto: Save_Crypto_Context_Init (0x005F0E14), SaveCode_GenerateCheckDigits (0x005F0408) and SaveCode_DecodeAndVerify (0x005EFE3C); the 0x200-byte source at 0x0072E93C and std_memcpy are visible. What exactly the 256 u16 entries encode (polynomial vs lookup) is still not proven, so 0.5.

name: maybe_Gfx_Trail_PushPathNode
signature: void maybe_Gfx_Trail_PushPathNode(Trail * self, int cellX, int cellY, int force)
summary: Adds a reached map cell to the trail's 16-entry path ring at +0xF0 (stride 0xC, index +0x1B0): if the cell differs from the current node it first validates/connects the step unless forced, then advances the ring index capped at 15.
evidence: Caller is now the confident Gfx_Trail_AdvancePathNode (0x005F3AF0) and the callee Gfx_Trail_TryConnectCell (0x005F3908), confirming the trail/path-ring role. The body still ends in bad instruction data (two truncated tails), so the post-advance bookkeeping is unverified; kept at 0.45.

name: maybe_Ui_ReleaseActiveSceneObjects
summary: UI teardown thunk: fetches the UI core through Ui_GetCore and calls Ui_SceneObject_Release on it, releasing the currently active UI scene objects. It performs no suspend/resume bookkeeping.
evidence: Both callees are confident names (Ui_GetCore, Ui_SceneObject_Release), but the only caller is now Sq_HashTable_Remove, i.e. it is used as a Squirrel-binding destructor callback rather than a UI flow step, so 'ActiveSceneObjects' is still an interpretation. Kept at 0.40.

name: maybe_Gfx_SceneSpriteSet_SetCharacterId
signature: void maybe_Gfx_SceneSpriteSet_SetCharacterId(SceneSpriteSet* self, unsigned int id, unsigned int arg3, int force)
summary: Selects the sprite set's active character id: stores it in f_1E, resolves the 0xD4-stride record and its redirect byte f_D1, then re-applies the preset with the (possibly redirected) id so the new character model/animation is built.
evidence: The previous evidence already noted 'AnimId' was too narrow: the callers select an actor/character, the redirect record f_D1 maps one character id to another, and Gfx_SceneSpriteSet_ApplyPreset rebuilds the model. No direct caller is listed (menu/table paths reach it indirectly), so the exact id domain stays at 0.45.

name: maybe_Field_GetActiveSubObject
summary: Accessor: returns self+0x98 when the embedded sub-object reports itself active through 0x0066A6BC, otherwise NULL. Callers use the result as an optional visual/effect object.
evidence: Three callers now exist (BG2DDisableMapEffect, Field_ApplySceneFade and maybe_Field2D_Scene_Create) and all null-check the result before calling methods on it, confirming the optional sub-object contract; which class owns +0x98 (field scene vs 2D background) is still unresolved, so the Field_ label stays at 0.45.

name: maybe_Field_HandleList_Ctor
summary: Constructs a small handle list: installs the local vtable 0x784304, allocates the 8-byte allocator wrapper (vtable 0x782B10) and a 0x94-byte reader object via func_0058C40C, so the list owns its allocator/handle pair.
evidence: Callers are now Ui3D_InitEffectPairFromRecord and maybe_Field_Scene_SpawnObjectsFromTableB, i.e. two different subsystems, which weakens the 'Field' label; the vtable install and the owned allocator+reader are visible, but both the reader constructor 0x0058C40C and the list's use stay unnamed. Kept at 0.42.

name: maybe_Battle_Unit_ValidateTarget
summary: Validates a battle target: locates it in the unit array at self+0xE8 (stride 0x2C8), looks up its action record through Game_GetDataManager, and returns 0 (reject), 1 (accept) or 2 (needs another check) after comparing the unit's slot/group/stat fields with the action's target criteria.
evidence: Callers are now Battle_SelectAiActions and Battle_ActionModel_UpdateAttachmentVisibility, and the body resolves action record fields via the data manager and compares ten target fields before returning 0/1/2. That supports target validation, but the return-code semantics and the criteria record are still inferred, so 0.45.

name: maybe_Actor_FindByField28
summary: Linear search over the field object manager's live entry array: returns the first non-null object whose record field +0x28 equals fieldValue, or NULL. The live set is derived from a byte id list and the manager's per-id present flags.
evidence: Callers are now Ui_Overlay_ApplySlotSetup and Ui_Overlay_ResolveSlotPlacement, both resolving a placement/anchor id, which fits searching a scene object by an id field; the companion 0x0062F514 matches +0x19 instead and no field name exists for either offset, so the offset-based name stays below 0.5.

name: Ui_Slot_IsLast
summary: Returns 1 when the resolved menu-cursor object's slot index at +0x270 equals the current slot count minus one, i.e. the cursor sits on the last slot. Used by the panel input handler to decide when to wrap/commit.
evidence: The resolver is now the confident Menu_Cursor_Resolve (0x006337CC), the comparison target is the count field under the UI context +0x130, and the body returns a real u8 value (not a void predicate stub). The caller is still the low-confidence panel input handler, so 0.5.

name: maybe_Ui_Slot_GetScale
summary: Float getter for field +0x2A4 of the object resolved by Menu_Cursor_Resolve, returning -1.0f when no cursor object exists. The decompiled C body shows no return because the value travels in VFP s0.
evidence: Disassembly at 0x00633A44 (look.py) is `vldr s16,[pc,#0x14] (-1.0f); bl Menu_Cursor_Resolve; cmp r0,#0; vldrne s16,[r0,#0x2a4]; vmov.f32 s0,s16` - a real float getter with a -1.0f default. Callers (Ui_Widget_DrawSelfAndChildren*, Ui_JockeyPanel_UpdateCursor) compare the result with a per-panel constant, but whether +0x2A4 is a scale, alpha or threshold is unproven, so 'GetScale' stays at 0.45.

name: Party_GetActiveMemberCount
summary: Returns the number of active party members: fetches the game work and delegates to Party_CountAliveMembers. Byte-identical to 0x0063A8A0, which keeps the return value; here Ghidra dropped it, making the body look void.
evidence: 0x0063A8A0 is now independently named Party_GetActiveMemberCount (0.65) from its assembly `mov r0,sp; bl Game_GetWork; ldr r0,[sp]; bl 0x00643504; pop {r3,pc}`, and 0x0063A820 has the same body with the same two named callees. The old 'GetActiveCount' was just a wording variant and 'Active' matches StateFlags bit 0, so the twin's name is the honest one.

name: maybe_Ui_TestPlacementFree
summary: Resolves the per-record handler through maybe_Ui_GetDefaultValue(record[4]), calls it with (record[0], record[1], record+2, point) and returns the inverted result, so 1 means 'cell is free / acceptable'.
evidence: Re-read with both callers now named - Ui_PlaceWidgetInFreeCell (0x004231B4) and Field_FindFreePlacementCell2D (0x00651A24), whose loops break on a 1 - the inverted handler result is a free-cell test. The handler table and record layout remain opaque, hence 0.45.

name: Gfx_Scene_QueryRect
signature: void Gfx_Scene_QueryRect(BoxQuery* query, const int* origin)
summary: Submits an oriented rectangle query to the scene: expands origin by the query offsets (f_54/f_58), sizes it by f_4C/f_50, takes the layer from query->f_38->f_AC and calls the scene rectangle query (0x002E5898) with the query's callback (f_5C) and user value (f_9C).
evidence: The 9 callers now include Field_FindFreePlacementCell2D, Field_GadgetDef_FindByName, maybe_Ui_Overlay_ReorderLastEntry and four area-overlap tests, so this is a shared scene helper, not Field-specific; the callees are Gfx_GetSceneSpriteContext and the scene query, and the body only builds the rect. The 'Field_' prefix was too narrow; 'QueryRect' is exactly what it does.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_GetLabelText
summary: Resolves a window label string: when the f_1C/f_1D/f_1E flags are clear it returns the inline text at self+0x22 for record id -1, otherwise looks up the record via the data manager and returns its relative string, or the inline buffer at self+0xC when the record carries the inline flag at +0xA; 0 when nothing applies.
evidence: No direct caller is listed any more, but the previous evidence's consumers (Ui_SaveWindow_LoadSlotName, maybe_Ui_Window_SetLabelFromSelection) both use the result as a string, and the body never touches reel/payout state (so the old casino name was wrong). The record getter 0x0063F2F0 is still unnamed, so 'label' remains an interpretation.

name: maybe_Item_GetGroupTag
signature: void maybe_Item_GetGroupTag(u32* out, u32 not, u16 itemId)
summary: Writes one of two static u32 item tags into *out: it treats the item as grouped when its record is missing or Item_IsSiblingRecord says the next id belongs to the same group, and then checks func_00381938(itemId) (0xFFFF = no mapping) to choose between the two tags.
evidence: Item_LookupRecord (0x0061BD4C) and Item_IsSiblingRecord (0x0066BE98) confirm item-group membership is being tested, and no item category field (+0x29) is read anywhere in the body, so the old 'ByCategory' was wrong. What the two global u32 values at 0x007AAF18/0x007AAF20 mean (and what 0x00381938 maps) is still unknown, hence 0.40.

name: Field_Actor_CheckRecordRectOverlap
signature: u32 Field_Actor_CheckRecordRectOverlap(int self, int id, u32* rect)
summary: Rect-overlap test against a scene record: resolves the record for self+0x5C through the scene sprite context, requires its first word to equal recordId, and tests the record's four u16 rect fields against the caller's rectangle, returning 1 on overlap.
evidence: Four callers are now named overlap users (Field_FindActorInRect, Field2D_Sprite_QueryChipAtEdge, Ui_Overlay_FindTargetUnderCursor, Ui_Window_TestActorOverlapAtSlot), and the callees Gfx_GetSceneSpriteContext / Field_HandleSet_ClearBits are named; the min/max comparisons over the four u16 fields are explicit. Returns a real u32 (not a dropped-return stub), so the predicate name is safe at 0.5.

name: maybe_Gfx_CmdBuf_CopyMarkedBlocks
signature: void maybe_Gfx_CmdBuf_CopyMarkedBlocks(uint32_t* dst, const uint32_t* src, int size)
summary: Copies a run of 0x80-word command-buffer blocks, writing a 0xEAD0FEAD marker after every 0x1FC-byte payload and a length-tagged header for the tail block; returns the new write cursor.
evidence: The marker 0xEAD0FEAD, the 0x1FC-word payload and the packed length header are visible and there is no PICA blend-register write, confirming the old Gfx_Pica_SetBlendMode name was wrong. No callers are listed and the only callee Gfx_GpuCmd_WriteTextureUnits is itself unverified, so 'CmdBuf' stays at 0.40.

name: maybe_Gfx_MeshChunk_WritePartMatrices
signature: void maybe_Gfx_MeshChunk_WritePartMatrices(GfxMeshChunkDraw* self, unsigned int** out, GfxMeshPartList* parts, GfxMeshBuffers* buf, GfxDrawTag* tag)
summary: Writes part matrices into the draw command stream in one of three forms: a single 0x30-byte matrix DMA bind (no flags), a gathered multi-matrix block for every listed part id (bit 1), or a palette-merged matrix array (bit 0) appended as a raw DMA block.
evidence: The three flag branches, the 0x30-byte matrix stride and the func_0050881C/func_0012515C/func_0012558C helpers are still the whole body, and the caller list is now 18 named draw/anim paths (UI layout animation, casino slot digits, field models) rather than one mesh code path. That makes it a shared matrix-block writer whose 'MeshChunk' owner is not proven, so 0.45.

name: maybe_Sound_Stats_SumPending
summary: Sums the integer counter at node-0x14 over an intrusive list, under the sound driver's monitor lock, and returns the total. Callers use it both from the frame profiler and from the sequence-player active-note update, i.e. it counts queued sound work.
evidence: Caller Sound_Profile_RecordFrame (0x0054DAA4) and the lock helpers Os_LockMonitor/Os_UnlockMonitor are named, and maybe_Sound_SeqPlayer_UpdateActiveNotes also calls it, supporting the queued-work count. The node geometry (-0x58 list node, counter at node-0x14) is still inferred and one caller (Ui_TextBlock_Update) does not fit, so 0.48.

name: maybe_Ui_Element_GetSlotIntValue
summary: Calls virtual slot +0x0C of the element interface stored at self+0x24 and returns its integer result converted to float. The decompiled body drops the float return; the call and the VectorSignedToFloat conversion are visible.
evidence: Caller Math_Vector_FixedToFloat (0x006F06CC, a UI tween command handler despite its name) calls this only when the tween target's f_2C flag is clear, i.e. it fetches the element's current value; the virtual slot and int->float conversion match. No caller uses it as a specific metric, and the float return was dropped, so the name stays generic.

name: Gfx_AtlasPage_GetSize
summary: Fills a {0, width, height} triple: when the cell source's virtual +0x50 reports layout kind 1, the width and height come from the global atlas page descriptor at 0x0073BAE4 (+0x18/+0x1C); otherwise the triple stays zero.
evidence: Callers are now Font_Atlas_LookupCell, Font_MapCharToGlyph, Font_GetGlyphAdvance, Text_BuildGlyphQuads and Bg2D_FindTexturePageByName, i.e. every consumer is texture-atlas/glyph layout, and the global page descriptor's +0x18/+0x1C are read as the page size. 'Ui_' was too narrow (Bg2D uses it too), so the prefix is corrected.

name: Field2D_MapChip_MapPointToCell
signature: void Field2D_MapChip_MapPointToCell(Cell* out, Field2DActor* self, unsigned int point)
summary: Maps a scene point to a 2D map cell: clamps it with Field2D_MapChip_GetColumnInfo against the actor's +0x78/+0x7C position and, when the point moved, transforms it through Field2D_Actor_TransformPosition; returns the cell or zero when the transform fails.
evidence: Callers now include Field2D_Actor_StepMoveTargets, Field2D_MapChip_CheckPathConnectivity, Field2D_Scene_RenderObjects and maybe_Field2D_Sprite_FindPath, and both callees (Field2D_Actor_TransformPosition, Field2D_MapChip_GetColumnInfo) are named. The out-cell is written in both branches, matching a map-point-to-cell mapping.

name: maybe_Field2D_Scene_GetStyleByte18
summary: Getter for the byte at +0x18 of the style/theme record reached through self+4 -> +0x298. The value is consumed by the 2D map scene builder and tile renderer.
evidence: Callers are now Field2D_Scene_BuildFromMapData and Field2D_Scene_RenderTileGrid, i.e. 2D map code, not text layout, so the old 'Text_Style' subsystem was wrong. The record chain and the +0x18 offset are certain, but what the byte encodes is not, so the offset-based name stays at 0.45.

name: maybe_Container_AppendCheckedEntry
summary: Appends an entry to an array builder: stores the pointer at build[2][count] and increments the count, then calls the builder's acceptance callback (through 0x0066846C and Field2D_Sprite_UpdateShadow) and rolls the count back when the callback rejects the entry.
evidence: Callers are now Field2D_Sprite_UpdateShadow and Field2D_Sprite_GetFootprintTile, and the push/increment/rollback sequence is unambiguous; but the acceptance callback name Field2D_Sprite_UpdateShadow does not fit a builder and the array-builder class is unnamed, so the generic 'Container_AppendCheckedEntry' stays at 0.40.

name: maybe_Text_SpanCursor_ClampLine
signature: int* maybe_Text_SpanCursor_ClampLine(int* out, int span, int* cursor)
summary: Clamps a text-span line index to the span's first/last line, writing 0 when the span starts left of the cursor position.
evidence: Callers are now the named Text_SpanCursor_Prev and Text_SpanCursor_Next, which supports the span-cursor role. The decompiled body is damaged (removed unreachable blocks and unaff_r7), so the exact clamp bounds and return pointer cannot be trusted; kept at 0.35.

name: maybe_Text_SpanCursor_PickRandomOffset
signature: int maybe_Text_SpanCursor_PickRandomOffset(int spanOwner, int* cursor, int lineStart)
summary: Picks a signed horizontal offset for a span: random width in [min,max+1] from Math_RandRangeInt, sign from a 0..2 roll, clamps the random/current/edge candidates, re-rolls once with the opposite sign if the result is zero, and returns the offset plus lineStart.
evidence: All three Text_SpanCursor callers (Init, StepMultiline, PeekVisible) remain, and Math_RandRangeInt is named; the span bounds are the u16 pair at owner+4+0x10/+0x12. However 5 of the 9 callers are Field2D scene build/render/placement paths, so this may be a shared random-offset-in-span helper and the Text_ prefix too narrow; kept at 0.40.

name: maybe_Field2D_Scene_GetStyleByte14
summary: Getter for the signed byte at +0x14 of the style/theme record reached through self+4 -> +0x298. Consumed by the 2D walk-trigger update and the map scene builder.
evidence: Callers are now Field2D_MapChip_UpdateWalkTrigger and Field2D_Scene_BuildFromMapData, both 2D map code, so 'Text_Style' was the wrong subsystem; the record chain and +0x14 are certain but the byte's meaning is not, hence 0.45.

name: Field_SceneTransition_IsBusy
summary: Returns non-zero while the scene-transition controller (game work +8 -> +0x74) reports a busy mode slot, by forwarding it to Camera_IsModeSlotBusy. With 90 callers across messages, effects, field spawning and UI it is the project-wide 'is a transition running' poll.
evidence: FACTS.md records the 90-caller shared helper; the caller list now confirms InnMessage, CreateEffect2D, IEMessageSetup, Field_Actor_CreateSprite and UI code all poll it. Assembly at 0x0066A720 is `mov r0,sp; bl Game_GetWork; ldr r0,[r0,#8]; ldr r0,[r0,#0x74]; bl Camera_IsModeSlotBusy; pop {r3,pc}` - it returns a value (Ghidra dropped the u32 return), and +0x74 is the scene-transition controller, so the old 'Battle_Ui_RefreshActionSlots' was both wrong subsystem and wrong action.

name: maybe_Field2D_Map_MarkLayerFlag
signature: void maybe_Field2D_Map_MarkLayerFlag(MapRoot* self, u32 layerId, int enable)
summary: Layer switch helper: when enable == 1 it scans the map's 8-byte layer pairs for layerId through func_0066AF84 and, on a hit, sets the 'layer changed' byte at self->f_3F0->f_27A4; it then always calls Field2D_Scene_AttachLayerObjects to refresh the map.
evidence: The tail call is now the named Field2D_Scene_AttachLayerObjects and the layer-pair scan is visible, so the refresh-after-layer-change reading holds. The middle of the body is damaged (a std_ConstructArray marked non-returning swallows the rest) and there are no callers, so 0.40.

name: maybe_Field2D_SpriteNode_Update
summary: Per-frame 2D sprite-node update slot: draws the node with Field2D_SpriteNode_Draw, then runs Field2D_Sprite_CheckViewBounds(self) so the view/callback step sees the new frame. Byte-identical twin at 0x00671AFC.
evidence: Both callees are now named (Field2D_SpriteNode_Draw, Field2D_Sprite_CheckViewBounds) and both are draw/update operations, so the old 'UpdateOverlaySprite' described only one side of a generic sprite-node update. There is no direct caller (vtable slot), so the slot's exact role stays at 0.45.
